```{r load}
# data from data-raw/chinook_sites_data.R and data-raw/chinook_sites_map.R
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("chinook_sites_values.rds"))
map <- readRDS(vd("chinook_sites_map.rds"))
prov <- v$provenance
sites <- v$sites
ids <- c("maxan", "swift", "naver", "gosnell")
stopifnot(identical(sites$site_id, ids))
name_of <- stats::setNames(sites$name, sites$site_id)

# colours come from the gq registry, so no hex literal appears in this article;
# assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_station.csv", package = "wet"))
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_map <- classes("chinook_sites_map", c("box", "target_gauged", "target_ungauged", "donor"))
pal_change <- classes("chinook_sites_change", c("extended", "carried"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(abs(x)), "%")
pct_of <- function(z) 100 * (exp(z) - 1)
and_text <- function(x) sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(x, collapse = ", "))
```

```{r numbers}
ch <- v$change
ch$pct <- pct_of(ch$change)
ch$pct_lo <- pct_of(ch$lo)
ch$pct_hi <- pct_of(ch$hi)
row_of <- function(id, w, route, s = "mean", group = "BULK") {
  r <- ch[ch$site_id == id & ch$group == group & ch$statistic == s & ch$window == w & ch$route == route, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
spw <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, row_of, w = "spawning", route = "carried"))
mig <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, row_of, w = "migration", route = "carried"))
# the answer: spawning-window flow lower at every stream, the migration window's range spanning no change
stopifnot(all(spw$pct < 0))
# "no stream shows a clear change by either route" in the migration window
mig_all <- ch[ch$group == "BULK" & ch$statistic == "mean" & ch$window == "migration", ]
stopifnot(all(mig_all$pct_lo < 0), all(mig_all$pct_hi > 0))
# "each gauged for under twenty years"
stopifnot(all(sites$obs_n[sites$site_id %in% c("swift", "naver")] < 20))
low_spw <- spw[spw$pct_hi < 0, ]
sc <- v$scores[v$scores$group == "BULK", ]
stopifnot(identical(sc$site_id, ids))
```

The article on [Maxan Creek](short-record-flow.html) used the R package
[`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) to fill in a five-summer gauge record
from nearby gauges and found its spawning-window flow lower now than before 1981. This
article asks whether that holds at three more Chinook streams, run the same way with the
method fixed in advance: Swift Creek at Valemount and Naver Creek near Hixon, each
gauged for under twenty years and filled in the same way, and Gosnell Creek in the Morice, which was
never gauged.

**The answer.** In the spawning window, flow in a typical year of 2011–2025 was lower
than before 1981 at all four streams, by `r pct(min(abs(spw$pct)))` to
`r pct(max(abs(spw$pct)))` from neighbours' departures alone; at
`r and_text(sub(" Creek$", "", name_of[low_spw$site_id]))` creeks the 90% range stays below no change. In the migration
window no stream shows a clear change by either route. The method scored about as well as at Maxan in the Cottonwood
and Morice boxes, and worse in the upper Fraser, where few long records sit nearby.

## Which streams?

```{r map, fig.height = 6.2, fig.cap = "The four streams, in British Columbia, and the boxes their neighbouring gauges come from. Each box is the same size as Maxan Creek's."}
tg <- map$targets
tg$part <- ifelse(tg$kind == "extend", "target_gauged", "target_ungauged")
gd <- map$gauges[!map$gauges$station_number %in% sites$target, ]
gd <- gd[!duplicated(gd$station_number), ]
gd$part <- "donor"
xy <- sf::st_coordinates(tg)
# labels set off each target, away from its own gauges
off <- data.frame(site_id = c("maxan", "swift", "naver", "gosnell"),
                  nx = c(25000, 30000, 25000, -25000), ny = c(30000, -45000, 30000, -40000),
                  hjust = c(0, 0, 0, 1))
lab <- merge(data.frame(site_id = tg$site_id, x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2], label = tg$name), off)
boxes <- map$boxes
boxes$part <- "box"
bb <- sf::st_bbox(map$bc)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = map$bc, fill = NA, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = boxes, aes(fill = part), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = gd, aes(colour = part), size = 0.9) +
  geom_sf(data = tg, aes(colour = part), size = 2.4) +
  geom_label(data = lab, aes(x + nx, y + ny, label = label, hjust = hjust), size = 3.1, fill = "white",
             alpha = 0.85, label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.12, "lines")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_map$values["box"], labels = pal_map$labels["box"], name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_map$values, labels = pal_map$labels[c("target_gauged", "target_ungauged", "donor")],
                      breaks = c("target_gauged", "target_ungauged", "donor"), name = NULL) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, nrow = 1), colour = guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 1)) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(bb[["xmin"]], bb[["xmax"]]), ylim = c(bb[["ymin"]], bb[["ymax"]]), datum = NA) +
  theme_void() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r use}
gauged <- sites[sites$kind == "extend" & sites$site_id != "maxan", ]
yr <- function(id, col) gauged[[col]][gauged$site_id == id]
# "inside the 1981–2010 baseline" and "before it"
stopifnot(yr("swift", "obs_first") >= 1981, yr("swift", "obs_last") <= 2010, yr("naver", "obs_last") < 1981)
# the Chinook records, from the tracked use report
u <- v$use
use_of <- function(stream) {
  r <- u[u$stream == stream, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
sw <- use_of("Swift Creek")
nv <- use_of("Naver Creek")
gs <- use_of("Gosnell Creek")
# "in most years since 1970" and "in most years since the mid-1980s"
stopifnot(sw$nus_first == 1970, sw$nus_use_years > (sw$nus_last - sw$nus_first + 1) / 2,
          nv$nus_first %in% 1984:1986, nv$nus_use_years > (nv$nus_last - nv$nus_first + 1) / 2)
# "a major spawning site within five kilometres of its mouth"
stopifnot(any(v$use_obs$stream == "Swift Creek" & grepl("^Major spawning", v$use_obs$activity) &
                v$use_obs$measure_m < 5000))
# "one survey that found adults, in 2001, and three provincial records of fish seen"
stopifnot(gs$nus_use == 1, gs$nus_first == 2001, gs$nus_last == 2001, gs$obs == 3, gs$obs_spawning == 0)
```

Each stream has recorded Chinook use. Fisheries and Oceans Canada's spawner surveys find
Chinook in Swift Creek in most years since 1970, and the provincial records place a major
spawning site within five kilometres of its mouth; they find Chinook in Naver Creek in most
years since the mid-1980s. Gosnell Creek's record
is thinner: one survey that found adults, in 2001, and three provincial records of fish
seen. The two gauged streams' records sit in different places from Maxan's five summers:
Swift Creek's gauge near the mouth ran `r gauged$obs_first[gauged$site_id == "swift"]`–`r gauged$obs_last[gauged$site_id == "swift"]`, inside the
1981–2010 baseline, and Naver Creek's at Hixon ran
`r gauged$obs_first[gauged$site_id == "naver"]`–`r gauged$obs_last[gauged$site_id == "naver"]`, before it.

## How has flow changed?

```{r change, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "Change in each Chinook window's mean flow, 2011–2025 against the years before 1981, with its 90% range. Blue: from neighbouring gauges' departures alone; orange: from the stream's own record filled in from neighbours."}
d <- ch[ch$group == "BULK" & ch$statistic == "mean", ]
d$site <- factor(name_of[d$site_id], levels = rev(name_of[ids]))
# the window labels from the Bulkley windows every site ran under
md_text <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  sprintf("%s %d", format(d, "%B"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
wb <- unique(v$windows[v$windows$group == "BULK", c("window", "start", "end")])
stopifnot(identical(wb$window, c("migration", "spawning")))
wlab <- stats::setNames(sprintf("%s (%s – %s)", c("Migration", "Spawning"), md_text(wb$start), md_text(wb$end)), wb$window)
d$window <- factor(wlab[d$window], levels = wlab)
ggplot(d, aes(pct, site, colour = route)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pct_lo, xmax = pct_hi), height = 0, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~window) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_change$values, labels = pal_change$labels, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Change in mean flow (%)", y = NULL)
```

```{r change-numbers}
ext <- ch[ch$group == "BULK" & ch$statistic == "mean" & ch$window == "spawning" & ch$route == "extended", ]
stopifnot(nrow(ext) == 3, all(ext$pct < 0))
morr <- row_of("gosnell", "spawning", "carried", group = "MORR")
stopifnot(morr$pct < 0, morr$pct_hi > 0)
# "smaller" than under the Bulkley windows
stopifnot(abs(morr$pct) < abs(row_of("gosnell", "spawning", "carried")$pct))
# "whose spawning window falls a month later": the Morice spawning window starts 25-35 days after the Bulkley's
start_of <- function(g) as.Date(paste0("2001-", v$windows$start[v$windows$site_id == "gosnell" & v$windows$group == g &
                                                                 v$windows$window == "spawning"]))
stopifnot(as.numeric(start_of("MORR") - start_of("BULK")) %in% 25:35)
# the ranking: largest at Maxan and Naver, smallest at Swift
rk <- spw$site_id[order(spw$pct)]
stopifnot(setequal(rk[1:2], c("maxan", "naver")), rk[length(rk)] == "swift")
err_factor <- exp(v$normal$err_abs_out[v$normal$group == "BULK" & v$normal$window == "spawning"])
# the citation section names routed PCIC as Gosnell Creek's typical flow
stopifnot(all(v$normal$pick == "pcic_routed"))
```

The spawning-window drop is largest at Maxan and Naver creeks and smallest at Swift
Creek. Filling in each gauged stream's own record
gives drops in the same direction (`r pct(min(abs(ext$pct)))`–`r pct(max(abs(ext$pct)))`).
Under the Morice's own Chinook windows, whose spawning window falls a month later than the
Bulkley's, Gosnell Creek's spawning-window drop is smaller, `r pct(morr$pct)`, and its range reaches
no change.

## How well does the method score?

```{r scores}
tab <- data.frame(
  Stream = name_of[sc$site_id],
  `Filled-in record` = sprintf("%.2f", sc$ols),
  `Gauges tested` = sc$ext_gauges,
  `Neighbours' departures` = sprintf("%.2f", sc$carried),
  `Gauges scored` = sc$carried_gauges,
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrr",
             caption = "Held-out scores in each stream's box: the median over gauges, where 1 is perfect and 0 is no better than the average year. Filling in a record is tested at the box's long-record gauges; Gosnell Creek has no record of its own to fill in.")
stopifnot(all(sc$carried >= 0.5), sc$ols[sc$site_id == "swift"] < 0.2)
# "the less certain of its two routes": Swift's filled-in range wider than its borrowed one, in both windows
width <- function(w, route) with(row_of("swift", w, route), pct_hi - pct_lo)
stopifnot(width("migration", "extended") > width("migration", "carried"),
          width("spawning", "extended") > width("spawning", "carried"))
```

Both routes are scored by hiding a gauge's own record and predicting it from its
neighbours. Neighbours' departures score at least 0.5 in every box, the bar set for
the method before any Maxan result. Filling in a record scores about as well as at Maxan in
the Cottonwood and Morice boxes and poorly in the upper Fraser, where only
`r sc$ext_gauges[sc$site_id == "swift"]` gauges have long enough records to test it. There,
Swift Creek's change from its filled-in record is the less certain of its two routes.

## Does snow explain it?

```{r snow}
sn <- v$snow[v$snow$group == "BULK" & v$snow$series == "carried" & v$snow$predictor == "swe", ]
sn_mig <- sn[sn$window == "migration", ]
sn_spw <- sn[sn$window == "spawning", ]
stopifnot(setequal(sn_mig$site_id, ids), setequal(sn_spw$site_id, ids))
# "at every stream": each migration slope's 90% range above zero
stopifnot(all(sn_mig$lo > 0))
r2_mig <- range(sn_mig$r2)
r2_spw <- max(sn_spw$r2)
stopifnot(r2_spw < min(r2_mig) / 2)
# the melt date, the other snow predictor, over the spawning window
melt_spw <- v$snow[v$snow$group == "BULK" & v$snow$series == "carried" & v$snow$predictor == "doy" &
                     v$snow$window == "spawning", ]
stopifnot(setequal(melt_spw$site_id, ids))
r2_melt <- max(melt_spw$r2)
stopifnot(r2_melt < min(r2_mig))
```

As at Maxan, migration-window flow at every stream follows the winter's snow. In
years with more peak snow over the stream's catchment, the departures borrowed for it are
higher, at all four with a 90% range above zero, and snow alone accounts for
`r round(100 * r2_mig[1])`–`r round(100 * r2_mig[2])`% of the year-to-year spread.
Spawning-window flow follows peak snow much less, at most `r round(100 * r2_spw)`% of its
spread, and the melt date at most `r round(100 * r2_melt)`%.

## Where could it be wrong?

- **Gosnell Creek's flow is never measured.** Its departures are tested only at the
  gauges around it, and its typical flow is `wet`'s published flow for the stream, which
  is off from measured flow, at the nearby gauges the water balance is not fitted to, by a
  typical factor of `r sprintf("%.1f", err_factor)` in the spawning window.
- **The windows are the Bulkley's** at all four streams. Only the Morice has its own cited
  windows; Swift and Naver creeks have none yet.
- **Each filled-in year rests on one neighbouring gauge**, and the earliest years on
  whichever single gauge reaches back that far.

## Software and citation

The flows in this article are from HYDAT release `r prov$hydat`; the published flow at
Gosnell Creek is routed PCIC's, as `wet` publishes it; the streams and catchments are the Freshwater Atlas's,
through `fwapg`. The data were bundled at `wet` commit `r prov$wet_commit`. How each
stream was chosen, and how the method is run and scored, is set out in
[`wet`'s research notes](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/research/chinook_sites.md).

```{r citation, results = "asis"}
cat(wet:::wet_software_cite(c("wet", "cd", "ggplot2", "gq", "sf")), sep = "\n")
```

Cite `wet` by the DOI above, which resolves to its latest release.

Data: daily flow from the Water Survey of Canada's HYDAT, release `r prov$hydat`; Gosnell
Creek's typical flow from the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium, University of Victoria
([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/): VIC-GL hydrologic model output
routed with Raven, PNWNAmet forcing), placed on the Freshwater Atlas by New Graph's fork of
`fwapg` (Norris, S. and Irvine, A. (2026), *fwapg, New Graph Environment's fork*,
<https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/tree/newgraph>) and published by `wet`
(build `r substr(v$normal$digest[1], 1, 7)`); the
Chinook windows from Gottesfeld, A. and Rabnett, K. (2007), *Skeena Fish Populations and
their Habitat*, Skeena Fisheries Commission, and for the Morice from Bustard, D. and
Schell, C. (2002), *Conserving Morice Watershed Fish Populations and their Habitat*,
<https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/Library/315091.pdf>; the spawner surveys from
Fisheries and Oceans Canada's New Salmon Escapement Database System (NuSEDS), release of
1 June 2026, <https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/c48669a3-045b-400d-b730-48aafe8c5ee6>,
and the provincial fish observations (Province of British Columbia, Known BC Fish
Observations and BC Fish Distributions); the stream network from the Freshwater Atlas
Stream Network (Province of British Columbia, 2021,
<https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/freshwater-atlas-stream-network>), held in a
database by Norris, S. (2024), *fwapg*, <https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg>.

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 800
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
